title: Luis Correa Named Entergy Texas’ Lineman of the Game
summary: From the deserts of Afghanistan to the electric grid of Southeast Texas, Luis Correa's career journey has been built on service. Correa, a journeyman lineman who works in Entergy’s Port Arthur service network, will step into the spotlight as the Lineman of the Game during the New Orleans Saints vs. Cleveland Browns matchup on Nov. 8 at the Caesars Superdome. title: Oak Ridge’s Transuranic Waste Processing Center gets upgrades
summary: The Department of Energy’s Office of Environmental Management has announced that part of the Transuranic Waste Processing Center (TWPC) at the Oak Ridge Reservation cleanup site has been remodeled and updated with new equipment. The upgrades will allow that part of the facility to process forms of transuranic (TRU) waste different from what it had processed in the past in order to support efficient site cleanup. The TWPC comprises four areas: a 5-line contact-handled glovebox, a 1,000-square-foot hot cell facility, a large box breakdown area, and a cask processing enclosure (CPE). The CPE is the area that has been updated.

title: First Fuel Loading Complete At China’s Sanao-2, Says CGN
summary: The loading of fuel assemblies into the core of the Sanao-2 nuclear power plant in the eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang has been completed, owner China General Nuclear (CGN) said. According to CGN, fuel loading was completed on 2 November, marking a major step towards nuclear-powered operation and commissioning. Sanao-2 is a 1,117-MW domestic Hualong One, or HPR1000, pressurised water reactor (PWR) unit. Construction began in December 2021.

title: NRC workshop addresses “bridge” between DOE authorization and NRC licensing
summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s Office of Advanced Reactors recently launched a series of workshops aimed at those who want to learn more about or will need to navigate the NRC’s licensing process. Dubbed “License to Launch,” the series began with primers on 10 CFR Parts 50, 52, the finalized 53, and the proposed 57.

title: Urenco touts first cylinder of LEU+ for commercial use
summary: Urenco USA has produced its first cylinder of uranium hexafluoride enriched to levels of uranium-235 between 5 and 10 percent, or LEU+. The company said that this is the first instance of commercial LEU+ production in “the Western world.” In May of this year, Urenco’s Capenhurst plant in the United Kingdom produced samples of LEU+ enriched to 7 percent U-235 in a trial run. Russia and China have explored the use of nuclear fuel enriched above 5 percent U-235 as well, according to the International Atomic Energy Agency.

title: Canada’s Bruce-5 Nuclear Plant Taken Offline For Major Component Replacement Outage
summary: The Bruce-5 nuclear power plant has been taken offline for its major component replacement (MCR) outage – the fourth unit to be refurbished under Bruce Power’s plan to renew six of the eight units at the Ontario site. The company said the 817-MW Candu pressurised heavy water reactor (PHWR) unit, which began commercial operation in 1985, was taken offline on 1 November. It said: “This represents the second half of the company’s privately backed MCR Project that will see units 3-8 renewed to provide clean, reliable energy for Ontario’s people, businesses and hospitals for decades to come, while also ensuring a dependable source of cancer-fighting medical isotopes for the world healthcare community.”

title: Amentum And Kyoto Fusioneering Sign MOU On Fusion In UK, Japan And US
summary: US engineering and energy technology company Amentum has entered into a memorandum of understanding with Kyoto Fusioneering to cooperate on nuclear fusion in the UK, Japan and the US. Amentum said the agreement with Kyoto Fusioneering, a Japan-based developer of fusion technologies, establishes a framework to strengthen both companies’ roles in advancing fusion energy commercialisation.
